topic: Interactions in Estuaries and Intertidal Zones
key_concepts: Estuaries form where river freshwater meets ocean saltwater
Estuary water is brackish from mixing fresh and salt water
Estuaries are called nurseries of the seas because many organisms reproduce there
Estuaries filter sediments and pollutants before freshwater reaches the sea
Estuaries serve as flood exit points during storms and heavy rains
Intertidal zones are coastal areas exposed to rising and receding tides
Waves, salinity, temperature, sunlight, and soil type are abiotic factors in these habitat
Kelp attaches to rocks with root-like structures to resist waves
Mangroves and blue crabs are adapted to changing salinity
Shallow estuary and intertidal waters allow sunlight to support photosynthesis
Soil type varies with wave strength and rocks and influences which organisms live there
Living things interact through feeding relationships that cycle nutrients and energy
